A design's TypeScript is compiled to JavaScript at build with `@swc/wasm`, legacy's compile with its options verbatim, so every design page receives JavaScript and the browser never loads `@swc/wasm-web` to compile it on each visit; the `0 x 0 x 0mm` placeholder state shortens toward legacy's, and the triangle desk's intermediate pose, which the M1 run tied to the same timing, is probed after. Two items, one on `/designs/bed-frame` and one on `/designs/5-12-13-triangle-desk`. Legacy compiled inside `getDesign` at build; here the build-time place is the designs generator, since this site's `getDesign` runs on the Worker per request under OpenNext's default cache, where a Node wasm binding cannot go, and the function's home is the generated module's question, the operator's on the designs index verdicts plan (`abb539b3555e` on `549ec777422c`), so the slice notes it there and files nothing new. Fable, since the placement is decided against the runtime. Record `0bc88eaf5493`; decisions `ee86d68a`, `2032533f`, `91cbeac8`.

## Work

- Legacy: `../node-modules/packages/designs/src/index.ts:44-66` at `fce357d`: `transform(designCode, { filename: designMeta.exports, jsc: { parser: { syntax: 'typescript' } }, module: { noInterop: true, strict: true, type: 'es6' }, sourceMaps: 'inline' })` with `designMeta.exports` rewritten from `.ts` to `.js` first; `packages/designs/package.json` pins `@swc/wasm ^1.6.6`. Current: `scripts/generate-designs-data.mjs:40-48` embeds each design's `.ts` text and its `exports` unchanged; `app/_lib/designs.ts:34-42` `getDesign` with its one-line comment naming this item; `@villagekit/product-kit@0.10.0 src/renders/index.tsx:26-39` picks the JavaScript renderer for a `.js` `exports` and the TypeScript one (`@swc/wasm-web` in the browser, `renders/typescript.tsx:24-70`) for `.ts`.
- `@swc/wasm` added beside `smol-toml` in `package.json`, the caret range every other dependency carries and the lockfile pinning it with its hash; the generator, after reading `code`, rewrites `meta.exports` to `.js` and transforms the code with legacy's options verbatim, so `designs-data.generated.ts` carries JavaScript with legacy's inline source maps and `exports` ending `.js`; `getDesign` keeps returning `{ code, meta }` and its comment names the generator. The generator's header (its page) says what it compiles and why, and that the output is deterministic for the pinned swc version, which the drift check `just generated` relies on.
- Why the generator and not `getDesign`, verified before the edit: the design page is prerendered through `generateStaticParams`, but `open-next.config.ts` configures no incremental cache and OpenNext's default is `dummy` (`node_modules/@opennextjs/cloudflare/dist/api/config.js:45`), so a prerendered page renders again on the Worker per request (the generator's header records the `readdir` incident), where `@swc/wasm`, a Node binding loading a wasm file of tens of megabytes from disk, cannot run within a Worker; the compile therefore belongs to the build step that already writes the module. The worker checks the two claims (`grep -n "dummy" node_modules/@opennextjs/cloudflare/dist/api/config.js`, `du -sh node_modules/@swc/wasm` after the install) and, if `getDesign` turns out to run at build only, writes the compile in `getDesign` as legacy's and says so in the Outcome.
- The placement: legacy's function compiled, this site's generator does; the difference is the generated module's, [[abb539b3555e]], the operator's: a note there says the compile lives in the generator and moves back into `getDesign` with the disk read if the operator chooses it. [[9d4e2e43543e]] closes: its Legacy is the build-time swc compile and its Current the raw TypeScript compiled in the browser, and after this slice the page receives JavaScript compiled at build by swc with legacy's options.
- [[e84e09089678]]: after the compile, probe `/designs/5-12-13-triangle-desk` at 1280 on `pnpm dev` at 1 s, 3 s and 6 s after load, three fresh loads, as the item's log did; if the desk draws its angled legs and separated shelves from the first frame, fix it citing this plan; if the pose persists, note the probe on the item and leave it `regression` for the record's finish.
- The generated module grows with the compiled code and the inline maps (174 KB now); the size after is recorded in the Outcome. `app/_lib/designs.test.ts` gains two assertions (below).
- Verify first: `grep -c "swc" package.json scripts/generate-designs-data.mjs` prints 0; `grep -c '"exports": "\./[a-z0-9-]*\.ts"' app/_lib/designs-data.generated.ts` prints 37.
- The record's Log and the note on [[9d4e2e43543e]] from the library slice say the compile lands in `getDesign`; this slice's note on [[abb539b3555e]] and a line on the designs index verdicts plan `549ec777422c` say it landed in the generator and why, so the operator's question on the generated module visibly includes the compile's home.

## Outcome

Shipped the compile of every design's TypeScript to JavaScript at build. `@swc/wasm` (1.16.2, Apache-2.0, caret range, 20 MB `wasm_bg.wasm`, its hash in the lockfile) is a dependency beside `smol-toml`; `scripts/generate-designs-data.ts` imports its `transform` (the CommonJS module's named export resolves under Node's type stripping, probed before the edit) and, after reading a design's code, carries legacy's block verbatim (`../node-modules/packages/designs/src/index.ts:47-66` at `fce357d`): if `meta.exports` ends `.ts`, rewrite it to `.js` and transform the code with `filename` the new `exports`, `jsc.parser.syntax` `typescript`, `module` `{ noInterop: true, strict: true, type: 'es6' }` and `sourceMaps: 'inline'`. The generator's header says what it compiles, why it compiles here and not in `getDesign`, and that the output is deterministic for the pinned version; `getDesign`'s one-line comment now names the generator instead of the item. `app/_lib/designs-data.generated.ts` carries `exports` ending `.js` on all 37 entries and the compiled code with legacy's inline source map; it grew from 174 KB to 631 KB (the source maps carry each design's source). `app/_lib/designs.test.ts` gains the two assertions the plan names, red before the generator changed and green after, and its `getDesign` test now reads `export var parts`, the compiled form (with no `jsc.target`, swc downlevels to its default, `es3` per `wasm.d.ts:682`, as legacy's options did). No visitor-facing text was written.

Two items are `fixed` with the outcome `plan 9d1770a4cd9e`: `9d4e2e43543e` (the compile) and `e84e09089678` (the desk's pose). The notes the plan asks for are written on `abb539b3555e` and `549ec777422c`: the compile lives in the generator and moves back into `getDesign` with the disk read if the operator chooses it. Both claims the plan asked to verify first held: `resolveIncrementalCache(value = "dummy")` at `node_modules/@opennextjs/cloudflare/dist/api/config.js:45` with `open-next.config.ts` configuring none, so `getDesign` renders on the Worker per request and the compile belongs to the build step; and `@swc/wasm` is a Node CommonJS binding (`wasm.js` with `require('util')`) loading a 20 MB wasm file from disk (`du` prints 0 under pnpm's hard links; `ls -la` prints 20248368 bytes), which no Worker bundle carries.

The desk's pose (`e84e09089678`), the finding of this slice: the intermediate pose is not a geometry state. A 400 ms screenshot series of the viewer from 0.4 s to 8 s after navigation, two fresh loads on each side (the scratchpad's `desk-series.mjs`, run from `audit/_probe/`), shows both sides drawing the same geometry from their first drawn frame (current's at about 2.0 s on the dev server, legacy's at about 1.2 s on the live deploy) and then turning under the viewer's auto-rotate, which advances once per rendered frame (drei's `OrbitControls` calling `update` with no time delta, the same code on both sides, the Parity reviewer's reading), so the angle at a given moment follows the frame rate and the two sides drift apart or catch up between loads. The stacked and overlapping shelves the M1 captures caught are the rotation seen edge-on, a window both sides pass through between about 2 s and 4 s after navigation; a capture lands in it or not by when the side's first draw came and how far it has turned since. The plan's probe at 1 s, 3 s and 6 s, three fresh loads: the spinner at 1 s, the angled legs and separated shelves at 3 s on every load (legacy's pose at 2.0 s), the rotation's later angle at 6 s, the same angle on both sides. Fixed citing this plan, with the mechanism in the Verdict, since the current side now draws its first frame at legacy's pose; the Verdict also says a pair on this route can still differ by the rotation's angle when the two captures are not at the same offset from each side's first draw, which the finish of this record and the parity gate should read as the viewer's auto-rotate and not as geometry.

Timings on `pnpm dev`, three fresh loads per route after one warming load (the scratchpad's `compile-probe.mjs`, `body.innerText` polled every 100 ms from commit): `/designs/bed-frame` shows `0 x 0 x 0mm` from commit and non-zero `Assembled Dimensions` (`1880 x 920 x 346mm`) 0.97 s, 0.99 s and 0.86 s after commit, where the M1 probe on the item read 8.8 s and legacy 1.7 s; `/designs/shelf-tower` (`680 x 400 x 1226mm`) 1.00 s, 0.96 s and 1.02 s; `/designs/5-12-13-triangle-desk` (`1280 x 498 x 1200mm`) 0.91 s, 0.97 s and 1.01 s. On every load the network log holds no request whose URL names wasm (the engine's `@swc/wasm-web` never loads) and the console holds no compile error, only emotion's kebab-case line (`92bb22f5456f`, open). Dev-server timings, not production.

Deviations from the plan's letter, with evidence:

- The Done when's bundle grep (`grep -rlE "@swc/wasm['\"]" .open-next/server-functions`) prints one path, `.open-next/server-functions/default/package.json`, the copied `package.json` whose `dependencies` list names the package; over the bundle's JavaScript (`--include='*.js' --include='*.mjs' --include='*.cjs'`) it prints nothing, `find .open-next -name wasm_bg.wasm` prints nothing and `.open-next/worker.js` holds no mention, so the server bundle carries no `@swc/wasm` code, which is what the line asks. `npx opennextjs-cloudflare build` completed with the dev server stopped by pid.
- `pnpm generate:designs` run twice writes byte-identical output (`cmp` clean), the plan's determinism check, read against a copy rather than `git status --porcelain` since the first run changes the module against `HEAD` by design; `just generated` is green against the staged module.

Verified: `timeout 900 just check` green with the dev server stopped (Biome, tsc, 91 tests in 5 files, `next build` with 61 static pages, the drift check against the staged module; its first run failed only at that check, before the regenerated module was staged); `kipu verify --warnings-as-errors` green. The screenshot pairs (`pnpm audit:pages`) on the three sampled routes at 375, 768 and 1280, 18 of 18 captured, looked at: the geometry renders on both sides with the dimensions text, the viewer, the preset select, the toggle and the button as before on 17 captures; `audit/designs__bed-frame/375/current.png` caught the spinner in the viewer with the dimensions already reading `1880 x 920 x 346mm`, the capture's moment on the dev server and not a state legacy lacks (the same route drew at 768 and 1280 and on the probe's three loads); the desk's angle differs by the capture's moment in the rotation; every other difference on the pairs is the shell's, an `upstream` item or a recorded one (the dev overlay's `1 Issue` badge is `92bb22f5456f`, the 768 wordmark wrap `1d2562d6b3bc`).

Reviews: three fresh Opus sub-agents (Standards, Spec, Parity), no critical findings. Taken: the generator's header now cites the ported block as the SHA-pinned GitHub URL (Standards); the desk Verdict names its probes' method instead of scratchpad paths that will not survive, and no longer claims the two sides turn frame for frame at a fixed offset (Spec, Parity); this Outcome's swc default target reads `es3`, `wasm.d.ts:682`, not es5 (Spec), and its pairs claim names the one capture that caught the spinner (Parity).
